name: Great Pyramid of Giza
description: The Great Pyramid of Giza, also known as the Pyramid of Khufu or the Cheops Pyramid, is the largest and oldest of the three pyramids on the Giza Plateau. Built as the tomb of Pharaoh Khufu during the Fourth Dynasty of the Old Kingdom, it is the only surviving Wonder of the Ancient World and remains one of humanity's greatest architectural achievements.The Great Pyramid was built around 2580–2560 BC during the reign of Pharaoh Khufu. It served as his royal tomb and demonstrated the remarkable engineering skills of ancient Egyptian builders. For more than 3,800 years, it was the tallest man-made structure on Earth.The Great Pyramid of Giza is one of the world's most iconic monuments and a symbol of ancient Egyptian civilization. Visitors can admire its immense scale, explore its internal passages, and experience one of the greatest engineering masterpieces ever built. A visit to the Great Pyramid offers an unforgettable journey into the history and achievements of one of the world's oldest civilizations.

name: Pyramid of Khafre
description: The Pyramid of Khafre is the second-largest pyramid on the Giza Plateau and was built as the tomb of Pharaoh Khafre (Chephren) during the Fourth Dynasty of the Old Kingdom. Although it is slightly smaller than the Great Pyramid, it appears taller because it stands on higher ground and still retains some of its original smooth limestone casing at the summit.The Pyramid of Khafre was constructed around 2570 BC as the royal tomb of Pharaoh Khafre, the son of Khufu. It formed part of an extensive funerary complex designed to honor the king and support his journey into the afterlife. The complex is among the best-preserved royal monuments from ancient Egypt.The Pyramid of Khafre offers visitors the opportunity to admire one of the best-preserved pyramids in Egypt. Its impressive architecture, surviving limestone casing, and proximity to the Great Sphinx make it an essential stop for anyone exploring the Giza Plateau and the legacy of the Old Kingdom.

name: Pyramid of Menkaure
description: The Pyramid of Menkaure is the smallest of the three main pyramids on the Giza Plateau. It was built as the tomb of Pharaoh Menkaure, the grandson of Khufu, during the Fourth Dynasty of the Old Kingdom. Despite its smaller size, it is admired for its elegant design and the use of high-quality granite in its.The Pyramid of Menkaure was constructed around 2510 BC as the final royal pyramid built on the Giza Plateau during the Fourth Dynasty. After Menkaure's death, parts of the pyramid complex were completed by his successor, likely Pharaoh Shepseskaf.The Pyramid of Menkaure offers a quieter and more intimate experience than the larger pyramids nearby. Its unique granite casing, well-preserved complex, and historical significance provide visitors with valuable insight into the final phase of pyramid construction during Egypt's Old Kingdom.

name: Bent Pyramid
description: The Bent Pyramid is one of the most unique and important pyramids in Egypt. Built for Pharaoh Sneferu, the founder of the Fourth Dynasty, it is famous for its unusual shape, where the angle of the pyramid changes halfway up. This distinctive design marks an important stage in the evolution of pyramid.The Bent Pyramid was built around 2600 BC during the reign of Pharaoh Sneferu. Historians believe the change in angle occurred because the original slope was too steep, causing structural concerns. Builders reduced the angle to ensure the pyramid's stability, making it a key step toward the construction of the later Red Pyramid, Egypt's first true smooth-sided pyramid.The Bent Pyramid is a remarkable example of ancient Egyptian engineering and experimentation. Its distinctive shape, well-preserved exterior, and historical significance make it an essential destination for anyone interested in the development of pyramid architecture and the achievements of the Old Kingdom.

name: Red Pyramid
description: Considered the first successful true smooth-sided pyramid.

name: Dahshur Pyramid
description: One of the famous pyramids in the Dahshur necropolis representing the development of pyramid architecture.

name: Step Pyramid of Djoser
description: The first large-scale stone structure in history designed by Imhotep.

name: Meidum Pyramid
description: An early transitional pyramid believed to have started as a step pyramid.

name: Pyramid of Unas
description: The first pyramid to contain the famous Pyramid Texts.

name: Black Pyramid
description: A Middle Kingdom pyramid built from mudbrick and named for its dark appearance.
